blocks.text: The most important guide. If you have a problem, it almost always starts here. Follow these steps before writing to us: in 90% of cases you will solve it in two minutes.
Pre-connection checklist

items: Bluetooth turned on on the phone.
GPS / Location turned on. Android requires location permission to scan for BLE devices. This is an operating system choice: the app does not use your location.
Chest strap wet at the contact points. Tap water or saliva, not gel.
No other app is connected to the sensor. Polar Flow, Polar Beat, Garmin Connect, Strava, Wahoo must be completely closed, not just in the background.
The sensor is NOT paired in the phone's Bluetooth settings. It must connect only through Stress Index, not through the system. If you paired it manually, remove it from the BT settings.

blocks.text: Step-by-step procedure

items: Put on the strap and wet the contacts well.
Open Stress Index.
Tap “Select sensor” on the home screen.
Wait for the sensor to appear in the list.
Tap the sensor name.
Wait for the “Connected” status with the blinking heart.
You are ready to measure.

blocks.text: Connection troubleshooting

blocks.title: The sensor does not appear in the list
items: Check that the strap is being worn: the sensor only activates on skin contact.
Close and reopen the app.
Turn Bluetooth off and on again.
On Android, check that GPS is on.
Check that no other app is connected to the sensor.
Remove the sensor from the phone's Bluetooth settings if you paired it manually.

blocks.title: It connects but no data arrives
items: Reposition the strap and wet the contacts again.
Try moving the phone closer to the sensor.
Close the app completely and reopen it.
If the problem persists, restart the phone.

blocks.title: It disconnects during the measurement
items: Do not move too far from the phone: 3 meters at most.
On Android, check that battery saver is not closing the app in the background.
Settings → Apps → Stress Index → Battery → Unrestricted.

blocks.title: Why are RR intervals needed?
blocks.text: HRV measures the variation between one heartbeat and the next with millisecond precision. A simple BPM value (beats per minute) is an average and loses all the information about variability. That is why you need sensors that transmit beat-to-beat RR intervals.
Setting up the environment

Quiet room, soft light, comfortable temperature. No phone calls, notifications silenced. The client should have been sitting or lying down for at least 2 minutes before starting, so the nervous system can settle.
Position

Seated with the back supported, feet on the floor, hands on the thighs. Or lying down. What matters is standardizing: always use the same position for the same client, otherwise comparisons between sessions lose their meaning.
Breathing
Natural. Do not tell the client to breathe slowly to relax, otherwise you invalidate the spectrum and get a picture that is not representative. Explain that they should breathe as they normally do.
Duration

items: **5 minutes** is the scientific standard (Task Force ESC/NASPE 1996).
**10 minutes** for a more stable analysis, less affected by momentary fluctuations.
**Free duration** for sessions during treatments, when you want to monitor the response over time.

blocks.text: What happens during the measurement

The app collects the RR intervals from the sensor, filters out artifacts in real time and, at the end, calculates all the parameters. Do not touch the phone during the measurement: let the app work undisturbed.

items.desc: A snapshot of the current state of the autonomic nervous system at rest.

5 minutes lying down, then the app tells you to stand up with a sound and a vibration, then 5 minutes standing. The app analyzes both phases and compares them.

Reduced autonomic reactivity, recovery after periods of illness (e.g. post-infectious syndromes), overtrained athletes, in-depth initial assessment. Every 4-6 weeks as a stress test of the nervous system.

blocks.text: Never compare an orthostatic test with a standard measurement: they are different things.

items.desc: The client breathes following a visual animation at a set rate (6 breaths per minute by default).
The app shows a sphere that expands (inhale) and contracts (exhale). The client follows the rhythm. Meanwhile the app calculates the coherence score in real time.
Cardiac coherence training, assessment of maximum vagal potential, search for the personal resonance rate. Useful for anxiety, insomnia, persistent pain, mental preparation.
It varies from person to person, between 4.5 and 7.5 breaths/min. You can test different rates in 2-3 minute sessions and see which one produces the highest LF peak in the spectrum.

blocks.text: Do not use coherence as an assessment measurement. To assess the client, always use the standard test. Coherence measures potential, not the current state.

Every score goes from 0 to 100. They are calculated by combining several HRV parameters with scientifically validated weights. They are the fastest way to read the client's state without diving into the individual parameters.
The 5 proprietary scores

items.title: Stress Index (0-100)
items.desc: How much pressure the nervous system is under. If it is chronically high, it indicates stress accumulated over time, not just at the moment of the measurement.

items.title: Recovery (0-100)
items.desc: Recovery capacity of the parasympathetic system.

items.title: Balance (0-100)
items.desc: Balance between sympathetic and parasympathetic. It is not 'higher = better': the optimal value is in the middle zone. Being too unbalanced in either direction is a problem.

items.title: Energy (0-100)
items.desc: Overall energy resources of the nervous system. Based on the total power of the HRV spectrum.

items.title: Adaptation (0-100)
items.desc: Recovery and adaptation capacity of the autonomic nervous system. The higher it is, the better the body absorbs the day's loads and the faster it returns to balance.

blocks.text: Composite Stress Index

A single 0-100 value that summarizes Stress, Recovery, Balance and Energy. You see it in the gauge at the top of the results. It is the number to track over time, especially when you compare several sessions of the same client.
The advanced parameters

Below the scores you find the details by domain (Time Domain, Frequency Domain, Non-linear, Geometric). Every parameter has a traffic light (green, yellow, red) based on reference ranges for the client's age and sex.

You do not need to know them all to use the app: the scores are enough in daily practice. The advanced parameters are there when you want to go deeper into a specific case or compare with the literature.

The morning HRV measurement is the simplest and most reliable way to understand how you are doing. It takes 5 minutes, seated or lying down, and gives you an objective snapshot of your autonomic nervous system.

blocks.title: Why do it every day
blocks.text: A single reading says little. It is the trend over time that is valuable. The more consistent you are, the more useful the data becomes.
When to do it

items: Within 30 minutes of waking up.
Before coffee, food, training.
Ideally after going to the bathroom.
The exact time matters little: consistency is what counts.

blocks.title: What to avoid before the test
blocks.text: Coffee, tea, cigarettes, intense training, a very hot or cold shower, stressful conversations.
How to do it step by step

items: Put on the strap: moisten the electrodes and wear it below the chest muscles.
Sit or lie down: choose a position and keep it the same every day.
Open the app: go to New Measurement, choose Standard Measurement, 5-minute duration.
Wait for the connection: within 10-20 seconds you will see the signal stabilize.
Relax and breathe: sit still, breathe normally, do not talk, do not look at the phone.
Wait for the 5 minutes: the app alerts you with a sound.

blocks.title: The secret is repeatability
blocks.text: Same time, same position, same sequence of actions.
The results

rows: how much pressure the body is under

blocks.text: How to interpret

items: **60-85**: optimal zone.
**40-60**: normal values, watch your habits.
**Below 40**: possible stress, poor sleep, illness.
**Below 25**: possible overtraining or exhaustion.

blocks.text: A single low value is no cause for alarm. What matters is the trend.
How to make it a habit

items: Keep the strap next to the bed.
Set a morning reminder.
Create a routine: after the bathroom, before coffee.
Use the 5 minutes in do-not-disturb mode.

blocks.text: Frequently asked questions

items.q: Can I do it after a sip of water?

a.text: Yes, water has no effect. Coffee does.

items.q: What if I skip a day?

a.text: Do not make it up, just resume the next day.

items.q: Can I do it in the evening?

a.text: Yes, but not instead of the morning one.

items.q: How long until the trend is useful?

a.text: 2 weeks to get started, 4-6 for a solid trend.
Do it anyway: seeing how it changes during illness is valuable.

s01What.body:
Cookies are small text files that a website stores in the visitor's browser to recognize them on their next visit or to remember a choice. Besides cookies, a website can also store information in other browser storage areas (localStorage), which stay on the device and are not sent to the server.

This page describes what the stressindex.io website and its Professional Area do. The Stress Index mobile app does not use cookies; the processing of its data is described in the Privacy Notice.
s01What.title: What cookies are

s02Technical.body:
The website only uses technical cookies, which are necessary for the pages to work or to store an explicit choice made by the visitor. No consent is required for these cookies.

• PROFESSIONAL AREA SESSION: cookies with the "sb-" prefix set by Supabase (the authentication service) when the professional signs in to the reserved area. They contain the session token, keep you signed in and are removed when you sign out. They are not set for visitors who only browse the public pages.

• LANGUAGE: the "NEXT_LOCALE" cookie, set when you choose a language from the switcher (IT / EN / DE). It remembers your preferred language for 12 months.

No other cookies are set by the website.
s02Technical.title: Technical cookies used by the website

s03Storage.body:
In the Professional Area some chart display preferences (time range, metrics shown, hidden series) are saved in the browser's localStorage so that you find them again on your next visit.

This information stays on your device, contains no personal data or measurements and is not sent to the server. It is removed by clearing the site data in your browser settings.
s03Storage.title: Preferences stored in the browser

s04Sentry.body:
To notice malfunctions, the website automatically sends a report to Sentry when a technical error occurs. This service does not set cookies and does not track browsing: it collects the type of error, the point in the program where it occurred, the website version and the browser type, together with a pseudonymous account identifier. Name, email, measurements and notes are not sent.

The details (data processed, storage in the European Union, 90-day retention) are in the section "Technical error detection" of the Privacy Notice.
s04Sentry.title: Technical error detection

s05NoProfiling.body:
The website does not use profiling cookies, advertising cookies, tracking pixels or traffic analytics tools that identify the visitor. There are no third-party cookies for social networks or advertising campaigns.

For this reason the website does not show a consent banner: none of the cookies used requires one. If tools requiring consent are introduced in the future, this page will be updated and consent will be requested before they are activated.
s05NoProfiling.title: No profiling or advertising cookies

s06Manage.body:
You can view, block or delete cookies at any time from your browser settings (usually under "Privacy and security" or "Site data"). Instructions are available in the help pages of Chrome, Safari, Firefox and Edge.

Please note that if you block technical cookies, signing in to the Professional Area will not work: without the session cookie you cannot stay signed in. If you delete the "NEXT_LOCALE" cookie, the website will again suggest the language based on your browser settings.
s06Manage.title: How to manage cookies in your browser

s01Parties.body:
Controller: the professional registered on Stress Index, with the details provided at registration ("Professional").

Processor: {company}, {address}, VAT and tax code {vat}, certified email (PEC) {pec}, email {privacyEmail} ("Performance Lab").

This agreement supplements the Terms of Service and applies to every Professional using Stress Index. In case of conflict, this agreement prevails as regards the processing of personal data. It is accepted with the dedicated checkbox at registration or re-acceptance; Performance Lab keeps the date, time, version and fingerprint of the accepted text.
s01Parties.title: Parties and scope

s02Roles.body:
1.1 Performance Lab provides the Professional with the Stress Index platform (app and professional area of the website) to collect, analyse and store heart rate variability measurements and other wellbeing parameters of their clients.

1.2 For data the Professional collects or receives in their activity (client records, in-studio measurements, measurements shared by the client, notes) the Professional is the controller and Performance Lab is the processor.

1.3 Performance Lab is an independent controller for: the Professional's account data; the account data of clients who register in the app; measurements that clients take with their own account; security logs. These processing activities are described in Performance Lab's privacy notices and fall outside this agreement.

1.4 The Parties exclude joint controllership: each decides alone on the purposes and means of its own processing. Sharing a measurement from the client to the Professional happens by decision of the client and is a disclosure between independent controllers.
s02Roles.title: 1. Subject matter and roles

s03Description.body:
• Purpose: allowing the Professional to measure, analyse and store wellbeing parameters of their clients and to produce reports.
• Nature: collection via sensor, calculation of parameters and scores, storage, display, PDF reports, comparison over time.
• Data subjects: the Professional's clients, adults, or minors with the consent of the holder of parental responsibility collected by the Professional.
• Data: identification and contact details; profile (physical activity, smoking, training level); inter-beat intervals and HRV parameters; wellbeing scores; sleep data (oxygen saturation, pulse rate); body composition; notes and tags of the Professional.
• Special categories: data concerning health (Article 9 GDPR).
• Duration: for the entire contractual relationship, with the termination rules in section 10.
s03Description.title: 2. Description of the processing

s04Instructions.body:
3.1 Performance Lab processes the data only on documented instructions from the Professional: this agreement, the Terms of Service and the Professional's use of the platform features.

3.2 The Professional hereby instructs Performance Lab to: (a) store the data with the providers listed at stressindex.io/legal/subprocessors; (b) perform the calculations and produce the reports provided; (c) make available to a client who links to the Professional with their own account the measurements concerning them; (d) apply the procedure in section 10 when the Professional's account is closed; (e) produce statistics on anonymised data under section 7.

3.3 Performance Lab informs the Professional if it considers that an instruction infringes data protection law.
s04Instructions.title: 3. Controller's instructions

s05ProfessionalDuties.body:
4.1 The Professional warrants a valid legal basis for every client. In all cases they obtain from the client explicit consent to the processing of data concerning health (Article 9(2)(a) GDPR), using the form provided in the app or an equivalent one, and keep it. Health professionals may also rely on Article 9(2)(h).

4.2 The Professional gives every client the privacy notice, uses the platform only to assess wellbeing within their own activity and competences, and does not enter data of people who are not their clients.

4.3 The Professional keeps their credentials safe, protects the device with a lock and notifies Performance Lab of any unauthorised access.
s05ProfessionalDuties.title: 4. Obligations of the Professional

s06ProcessorDuties.body:
5.1 Confidentiality: persons authorised by Performance Lab are bound by confidentiality and trained in data protection.

5.2 Security (Article 32 GDPR): encryption in transit and at rest; isolation of each Professional's data with row-level access policies; authentication for every access; obfuscation of the app code; logging of administrative access in an immutable log, with notification to the Professional; automatic backups. Performance Lab staff access identifiable data only for support or incident handling, upon documented request, to the minimum necessary and with logging; software development tools work on pseudonymised data.

5.3 Assistance: Performance Lab helps the Professional respond to data subject requests through the platform's export and deletion features and, when these are not enough, acts within 10 days. Requests that clients send directly to Performance Lab about data processed for the Professional are forwarded within 3 working days.

5.4 Impact assessment: Performance Lab provides the Professional with the information needed for their assessment, including a summary of its own.

5.5 Data breaches: Performance Lab notifies the Professional of any breach affecting their data without undue delay and in any case within 48 hours of discovery, with the information in Article 33(3) GDPR, and cooperates in notifying the supervisory authority and the data subjects.

5.6 Audits: Performance Lab makes available the information needed to demonstrate compliance with Article 28 and allows audits, including by an independent auditor, with 30 days' notice, at most once a year except after an incident, at the Professional's expense.
s06ProcessorDuties.title: 5. Obligations of the processor

s07Subprocessors.body:
6.1 The Professional gives general authorisation for the providers listed at stressindex.io/legal/subprocessors, with location, service, data location and safeguards.

6.2 Performance Lab announces any addition or replacement by email 30 days in advance. The Professional may object on legitimate grounds within that period; if no solution is found they may terminate without penalty. Silence counts as authorisation.

6.3 Performance Lab imposes on every provider obligations equivalent to those of this agreement and remains liable to the Professional for their performance.
s07Subprocessors.title: 6. Sub-processors

s08Anonymous.body:
7.1 The Professional authorises Performance Lab to anonymise the data, irreversibly removing every identifying element, and to use the anonymised data for statistics, improvement of the algorithms and publications.

7.2 No other use of the data for Performance Lab's own purposes is allowed. Processing of identifiable data for Performance Lab's purposes may only take place with consent collected by Performance Lab from the client with an account, and only concerns data of which Performance Lab is the controller.
s08Anonymous.title: 7. Statistics on anonymous data

s09Transfers.body: The data are stored in the European Union. Any transfer to third countries takes place only through authorised providers, on the basis of an adequacy decision (including the EU-US Data Privacy Framework for certified providers) and, in addition, the European Commission's standard contractual clauses, with supplementary measures where needed.
s09Transfers.title: 8. Transfers outside the European Union

s10ClientLink.body:
9.1 When a client of the Professional links with their own account, the client decides whether to share their measurements and may revoke sharing. Measurements received before revocation remain available to the Professional as controller.

9.2 The Professional acknowledges that a client with an account also sees in their profile the in-studio measurements concerning them, in fulfilment of the rights of access and portability.
s10ClientLink.title: 9. Link with the client's account

s11Termination.body:
10.1 The Professional may export their clients' data at any time in PDF and CSV.

10.2 When the Professional's account is closed: (a) the platform offers a full export before confirmation; (b) measurements of clients who have their own account are offered to the client, who may keep them in their profile with explicit consent within 30 days, otherwise they are deleted; (c) data of clients without an account are deleted, after an invitation to create an account within 30 days if the Professional requests it; (d) the account and remaining data are permanently deleted, except backups, overwritten within 35 days, and pseudonymised security logs, kept up to 12 months.

10.3 The Professional remains responsible for any retention obligations of their profession, to be met through the export.
s11Termination.title: 10. Termination and deletion

s12Liability.body:
11.1 Each Party is liable for damage caused by processing in breach of the Regulation within the limits of Article 82 GDPR. Performance Lab is liable only for damage arising from failure to comply with the processor's obligations or the Professional's lawful instructions.

11.2 Between the Parties, except for wilful misconduct or gross negligence and except where liability cannot be excluded by law, Performance Lab's liability is limited to the amount paid by the Professional in the 12 months preceding the event.
s12Liability.title: 11. Liability

s13Final.body:
12.1 The agreement has the same duration as the Terms of Service. The clauses on confidentiality, deletion and liability survive termination.

12.2 Performance Lab may update the agreement to reflect laws, decisions or changes to the platform, with 30 days' notice; material changes require new acceptance.

12.3 Italian law applies; the court of {court} has exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute.

athletePage.swcNote: Resting HRV measurements only (standard test): orthostatic, coherence, long sessions and workouts are excluded. threshold.methodNote: Threshold estimate based on DFA alpha1 (Rogers et al. 2021). DFA alpha1 alone tends to place the first threshold a few beats higher than a laboratory test. For maximum precision the reference remains the cardiopulmonary exercise test.
threshold.noEstimate: Test run without threshold estimate: the sensor was not transmitting the RR intervals needed for DFA alpha1.
threshold.noSignal: Signal not sufficient to estimate the thresholds
threshold.noTests: No incremental test with threshold estimate has been run yet.
threshold.noneSaved: No thresholds saved to the profile: they are saved from the app, from the results of a test with a reliable estimate.

reasons.inconsistent: VT2 is not above VT1: inconsistent estimate, not saved.
reasons.lowR2: The line fits the data poorly (R² below 0.6).
reasons.noDescendingTract: Alpha1 does not show a steady decline as HR rises.
reasons.notEnoughData: Less than 10 minutes of valid data after the warm-up.
reasons.sensorNoRr: The sensor was not transmitting RR intervals.
reasons.tooManyArtifacts: Too many windows discarded for artifacts: the strap was loose or dry.
reasons.vt1Extrapolated: The estimated HR would fall more than 5 bpm outside the observed data: no extrapolation.
reasons.vt1NotReached: Intensity reached was insufficient: alpha1 never dropped below 0.75.
reasons.vt2Extrapolated: The estimated HR would fall more than 5 bpm outside the observed data: no extrapolation.
reasons.vt2NotReached: The test did not reach the second threshold: alpha1 never dropped below 0.50.
